Sierra Ops se présente sous la forme d'un VN plutôt classique mais qui une fois passé le prologue le jeu s'étoffe largement avec des combats spatiaux, une amélioration possible du vaisseau et  des pts de déploiement pour choisir vos missions secondaires dont le coût en point varie et qui vous donneront des bonus différents lors des missions de campagne.

D'un point de vue VN on trouve des personnages correctement écrit et un univers très riche mais malheureusement des références à des événements antérieurs à l'histoire ce qui certes donne de la profondeur au tout mais peut être frustrant (dites nous ce qu'il s'est passé à [spoiler] Damascus [/spoiler] par pitié!), j'espère que tout sera expliqué plus tard.
Il est a noté qu'il y a une grande différence sur le déroulé de l'histoire et les personnages rencontrés selon un certains choix dans l'histoire. Vous ne rencontrerez certains personnages importants que si vous prenez certaines voie. C'est également bien amené et ça encourage à rejouer plusieurs parties.

Pour les batailles spatiales, elles se déroulent en vue du dessus et se basent sur un système de priorité. Vous avez des groupes d'armes à qui vous attribuez des types de cibles prioritaires (les groupes d'armes sont modifiables entre les missions). Vous guidez votre vaisseau en lui indiquant une position où se rendre et en choisissant un mode de déplacement (normal pour se déplacer comme un navire, straffe pour maintenir son orientation pratique pour garder ses cannons face à l'ennemi, etc).

Le jeu n'est pas encore fini (2 épisodes sur 4 pour le moment) mais il est très prenant, bien écrit et surtout amélioré avec le temps;pour y avoir joué une première fois plusieurs années avant et maintenant ça n'a rien à voir, même les parties déjà existantes sont remises à niveau.
Je recommanderai donc sans hésiter.

For me this game just hits an area that I really enjoy so I am going to start with listing out why it just grabs me. Note that this game isn't perfect, but a lot of these things I believe can be improved upon with time. I don't really want to spoil so I am going to try and not name any of the characters or get too specific.  

1. The concept: I am a sucker for syfi and space in general, I love the ideas and scale that it comes with and to me the game captures that part pretty well. Its a a very solid space drama in my eyes. 

2. The World: I feel like I am in a believable alternate universe that had its own things going on before I entered it and will have things going on after I interact with it. The team does a good job setting up the world to feel alive through the characters and interactions between them. For lore nerds they also have a compendium of terms and history summaries about events that happen in the world, characters and even the technology. This feature reminds me of the codex in Mass Effect which I loved. 

3. Uniqueness: The only other game that I have played or know about tackling this specific type of genre is the Sunrider games, I for one think this format is very under utilized. Like a space visual novel with rpg and rts elements, really hits all the genres of games I enjoy playing. 

3. I like the developers: I don't know them personally or anything but if there is one thing I have learned through the development of this game is that they don't give up easily. They should be proud of that. 

4. Impact: The thing this game does best is present you with a load of choices that you have to make that have an actual impact on how things go. Especially as it picks up in episode two their is a lot of considerations you have to make in your decision making. For example, your companions at least in the second episode are decided entirely on what you decide to do at the end of episode one. That leaves a lot of room for replay ability as well. You can easily play this game as three separate save files and experience enough unique content to not feel like they are to samey 

5. Characters: I personally like all the characters so far, they are well written and have stuff going on in their lives. There are a few of course (and by few i mean like 2-3) that are a little cliche and they have there tropes that kind of stand out as weird or slightly illogical. But like what game or visual novel doesn't. Plus that doesn't matter as long as they are utilized well in the story, and so far I would say all but one fulfill that goal. Plus the one character I am thinking of doesn't really get much screen time to make an impact yet anyway. 

6. Potential: I want to get this one clear that this is a far more personal one, everyone judges value and worth differently but especially after the release of episode two I firmly believe there is enough there to be worth the 15 dollars. Not only that but the improvements the team has made and the communicative stance that the devs are taking makes me really endeared to this games development. Like if I was rich I would probably fund this game personally just so that I could play the end product quicker. I have embraced this game flaws and all because I have judged the good to far outweigh the bad. Plus the bad to me is more a symptom of being new developers than a genuinely unfixable problem. You can improve the combat, you can fix bugs, and you can improve the U.I. Sometimes all it takes is a bit of feedback and experience. No one starts perfect but I believe they have started genuinely better than most. Plus as long the attitude and passion that the developers have stay where it is now I firmly believe they will release the full product and that it will be pretty damn good.

Sierra Ops is a mix of a combat, visual novel, and RPG meeting together in space to create an interesting story that has taken the time needed to construct some much-needed world building to establish the world you, the player, are inhabiting, the reasons behind the conflict that erupts, and you're forced into.

In Sierra Ops, you are Junius Fahrenheit trying to overcome a traumatic moment from your past while leading the latest developed vessel into an unexpected war that Sierra itself wasn't built for. Despite the strength and power of the vessel you're given, can you win a war, stay true to your ideals, and overcome the chains of your past that keep Junius closed off to others?

Sierra Ops' combat feels decent. You're able to customize the weapons your ship, Sierra, has and even design new weaponry depending on what blueprints you acquire. This has the potential to give the player multiple options on how to develop their Sierra and the actual combat feels fun to me. Having double speed is good and allows players to cut down on time in battle, especially when you're closing the distance or cleaning up to finish the battle. You're also able to take on a wingman ship that will level up after enough combat, so try to keep them alive yeah?

The visual novel aspect sees you deciding who to hang out with during free time in order to better your relationship with them. It sees you deciding who the first few people on your ship will be with one of the first destination choices in the game, opening several paths of replayability with their own pieces of world building and stories to uncover. I found it quite enojoyable when one character pointed out an important person on the enemy side from past history that not only did some world building, but made me go "I know that guy!" when I saw him later on in another path. It was an enjoyable moment where I was able to use information acquired from one character on a side mission to realize the identity of an enemy before the characters themselves realized it due to being on a different path.

The RPG aspect is a mix of the previous two with your choices impacting the war. It might not seem like it at first glance, but in order to win this war for the UTV your mission choices matter. Whichever missions you choose can impact the war to various degrees that aren't immediately clear. Some missions have larger impact than others, but all do impact main missions you partake in. You cannot do every side mission per segment and thus you'll need to weigh your options on which is more important to you. A mission that could better your relationship with a certain character? A difficult, but valuable supply mission  that will surely impact the war and the view of your peers? Your options are limited, Captain, but you must make a decision. You could also choose to forgo the side missions entirely, at your own peril.

Personally I've enjoyed Sierra Ops so far and bought the Season Pass quite some time ago. Although I need to play more and finish some paths up to their current completion, I've enjoyed the story and missions I've played so far. They're actively updating the game with bug fixes, some additions, and updates for the next two bigger episodes. Can't wait for their release!

Good Visual Novel style Space Opera with action-focused combat. Even though the Space Opera setting has been done in many places, you can feel the world building at play, with all the elements working with or against other parts. If you're big into sci-fi world building, there's a lot to like here. The characters do feel like they've lived in the world for awhile. Fair warning: the story is a bit of a slow burn. While it does start off with a critical moment, it takes awhile for it to be put in context and for the story to get going proper.

The strategy action bits are pretty fun with each mission being crafted to have different objectives, though I wish there were a free-play mode where you can play the action games freely. At this time there doesn't feel like a whole lot of enemy variety, though I suspect it will get fleshed out more over time.

All in all, purchase this if you enjoy:
-Visual Novel elements
-Varied character archetypes
-Space Operas with good world-building
-Space strategy-action games (smaller scale of a typical RTS, more small-unit tactics)
